previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and epigastric abdominal pain following a medication error in which she mistakenly took fluconazole instead of prednisone. This led to under-treatment of her chronic graft-versus-host disease, requiring re-initiation of high-dose prednisone. The increase in steroids likely worsened steroid-induced gastritis, causing her symptoms. A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis showed no acute pathology. She was treated with increased pantoprazole and initiation of sucralfate, with symptom improvement. Her transaminitis remained at baseline and was attributed to GVHD. Chronic hip pain was managed with oxycodone. Medication reconciliation was completed with patient and family education. She stabilized and was discharged home with updated medication instructions and follow-up plans.

INDICATION:  Right-sided abdominal pain.

COMPARISON:  CT ___.

FINDINGS:  Supine and upright views of the abdomen were obtained.  The bowel
gas pattern is nonspecific without evidence of obstruction or ileus.  There is
no free air. Large fecal loading is noted in the ascending colon.
Cholecystectomy clips are seen in the right upper quadrant. Mild degenerative
change in the lower lumbar spine is incompletely evaluated.  A surgical clip
projects over the pelvis, unchanged from CT ___.

IMPRESSION:  No obstruction or free air.

INDICATION:  Chronic GVHD with abdominal pain.

COMPARISON:  AXR ___ and CT ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images from the lung bases to the iliac crests
were obtained with oral and 100 mL Optiray intravenous contrast.  Coronal and
sagittal reformats were displayed with 5-mm slice thickness.

CT ABDOMEN:  The visualized lung bases are clear.  There is no pleural or
pericardial effusion.  

The liver, spleen and bilateral adrenal glands are normal.  The gallbladder is
surgically absent. There is some fatty infiltration of the pancreas, which is
otherwise unremarkable.  The kidneys enhance symmetrically and excrete
contrast promptly without hydronephrosis.  The visualized portions of the
small and large bowel are normal in course and caliber.  There is large fecal
loading in the ascending colon as noted on abdominal radiograph ___.
There is no free fluid and no free air.  No pathologically enlarged mesenteric
or retroperitoneal lymph nodes are present.  The aorta is of normal caliber
throughout.

BONE WINDOWS:  No lytic or sclerotic lesion suspicious for malignancy is seen.
Degenerative change is noted in the lower thoracic and upper lumbar spines.

IMPRESSION: No acute intra-abdominal process to explain patient's symptoms.
Note that a pelvic etiology for patient's symptoms cannot be evaluated on this
study.

INDICATION:  Abdominal pain.

AXR ___ and CT ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images were acquired from the inferior renal
poles to the pubic symphysis without new contrast administration.  Oral
contrast and IV contrast were administered for CT abdomen three hours prior.
Coronal and sagittal reformats were displayed with 5-mm slice thickness.

CT PELVIS:  The visualized loops of small and large bowel are normal in course
and caliber without obstruction or bowel wall thickening. The rectum, bladder,
and uterus are normal. Scattered diverticula are seen in the sigmoid colon
without inflammatory changes. There is no free fluid and no free air. No
pathologically enlarged mesenteric, retroperitoneal, pelvic or inguinal lymph
nodes are identified.

BONE WINDOWS:  No lytic or sclerotic lesion suspicious for malignancy is seen.

1.  No acute intra-pelvic process.
2.  Diverticulosis without diverticulitis.

STUDY:  Abdomen supine and erect films, ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ woman with right upper quadrant pain.  Evaluate
for free air.

FINDINGS:  Comparison is made to previous study from ___.

There is no free intra-abdominal gas identified.  Contrast and stool seen
throughout the colon, which is not dilated.  No dilated loops of small bowel
are seen.  Surgical clips are seen within the right upper abdomen and within
the pelvis.  The bony structures are intact.  There are some degenerative
changes of the lower lumbar spine as well as bilateral hip joints.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No free air in the abdomen.

2.  Non-obstructive bowel gas pattern with contrast and stool seen throughout
the colon and rectum.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with BMT.  Worsening hepatitis, query biliary
process.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1- and T2-weighted images were acquired on a 1.5 T
magnet.  A breath-hold independent technique was performed before and after
injection of 0.1 mmol/kg gadolinium-DTPA.

FINDINGS:  The liver parenchyma is normal, without focal lesion.  No biliary
dilatation is present.  The patient is status post cholecystectomy.  A dropped
clip is noted adjacent to the right kidney.

There is diffuse pancreatic atrophy.  A number of pancreatic cysts are also
present in the body and head, the largest measuring 1 cm (series 12, image
58).

The kidneys, adrenal glands and spleen are normal.  No intra-abdominal fluid
collection. Marrow signal is unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
1. Status post cholecystectomy with no evidence of biliary dilatation or
intrahepatic ductal filling defect.

2. Pancreatic cysts, the largest in the head measuring 1 cm.  Interval
follow-up in one year advised.

transplantation, admitted with varicella zoster.  Persistent right upper

2.  No evidence of free air in the abdomen.
